teaching: A way can be a guide, but not a fixed path: people start from different places, there is no formula for greatness, and a religion too rigid and encrusted from use is not the Way, which moves like wind (Tao Te Ching, Chapter 1, Thomas Cleary translation).
youtube_title: A Way Can Be a Guide, Not a Fixed Path

word_overrides.why: medium.en hears 'Away'; it is Cleary's 'A way' (envelope onset 181.14)
medium.en starts 'The' at 263.16 in room tone; the envelope onset is 263.60 (large-v3 hears no 'And' before it)
medium.en starts 'The' at 331.50 in the pause; envelope onset 331.94
the cut sits between 'path' (its 'p' closure is the dip at 306.18, the vowel 306.22-306.38) and 'So' (306.42); medium.en puts 'So' and 'what' both at 306.64

phrases: The minute you try | and put it into

image.note: a scholar absorbed in playing the qin: 'the human artistic, scientific, or creative spirit'
travelers on the zigzag plank road: 'A way can be a guide, but not a fixed path. The truth of this is obvious' (on the join)
the Thirty-Six Poetic Immortals, each one different: 'People come from many different backgrounds… inclinations… conditioning'
the rich man and his guests at their feast: 'They have different resources' (on the join)
the beggar Lazarus lying outside the feast: '…resources' (the same painting: rich, then poor)
a painter at his easel, a boy drawing beside him: 'There's not a fixed path to artistic greatness or to scientific discovery' (on the join)
Daubigny's The Oak Tree and the Reed: the rigid oak torn down by the storm, for 'too fixed, too formulaic, too rigid' (against the bamboo that bends, at the end)
bamboo bending in the wind: 'The way is much more like nature, like wind… not on a fixed path' (on the join; under the end-card dissolve)
